text: Ready, little explorer? Our pretend rocket is visiting the Moon. Three, two, one, lift off!
Hello, Moon! Those round dents are called craters. Let's look for a big one and a little one.
Long ago, space rocks bumped into the Moon and made many craters. Make a little circle with your finger.
The Moon pulls us down less strongly than Earth does. Astronauts can take bouncy steps there. Wiggle your fingers like tiny feet!
There's Earth, our home! The Moon travels around Earth. Let's wave to our blue planet.
Mission complete! We discovered craters and practiced pretend Moon steps. You are a wonderful crater detective!
Our pretend rocket has a mystery to solve. How does the Moon look bright? Let's investigate together!
The Moon is Earth's space neighbor. Sometimes we can see it in the daytime, too. Hello, neighbor!
The Sun makes its own light. Some sunlight reaches the Moon. We'll explore with pictures and never look straight at the real Sun.
Sunlight bounces off the Moon toward us. The Moon does not make its own light. Mystery solved!
From Earth, the bright part of the Moon can look different on different nights. The Moon itself stays round.
You solved the moonlight mystery! When you're outside with a grown-up, see if you can spot the Moon.
Pack an imaginary picnic! Our pretend rocket will peek at Earth from space, then bring us home.
Look at all that blue! Oceans cover much of Earth. Can you point to a blue part of our picture?
Earth has land, too. People, plants, and many animals live on land. Pretend to wave to a tiny tree below.
Those fluffy white shapes remind us of clouds. Earth has air around it. Take a gentle breath with me.
Our pretend rocket is coming home. On Earth we have water to drink and air to breathe. What a special home!
Picnic time! We found oceans, land, and clouds. Let's care for our home planet together.
We have a pretend delivery for Earth: a good-morning wave and a good-night wave. Let's find where they belong!
The Sun lights one side of Earth at a time. That side has daytime. Say, good morning!
Earth slowly spins. Imagine turning a ball in your hands. A place on Earth turns toward the sunlight, then away.
When our part of Earth faces away from the Sun, it is nighttime. Give a little good-night wave.
Our pretend delivery is done! Earth keeps turning while we play and while we sleep.
Day and night happen as Earth spins. We delivered both waves. Good exploring, little space friend!
Beep, beep! Our pretend rocket is taking a robot explorer to Mars. Can you make a little robot beep?
There's Mars! Rusty minerals in its dusty ground make it look reddish. Point to our red planet picture.
A rover is a robot that drives and explores. Real rovers help scientists study Mars. Roll your hands like little wheels.
Mars has rocks, hills, and dusty ground. Our pretend rover stops to look carefully. Scientists learn by noticing things.
Beep! Our pretend rover sends a message to Earth. We found a rocky, reddish world!
Great exploring! Mars is a planet, and rovers are robot explorers. Give our pretend rover a happy beep!
Our pretend rocket is visiting Mars to find its two little moons. Let's count together on our trip!
Mars is smaller than Earth. Its dusty surface looks reddish. Hello, Mars! We're here to meet your moons.
Mars has a moon called Phobos. That's one moon. Hold up one finger if you like.
Its other moon is called Deimos. One, two! These moons are small and lumpy, not smooth round balls.
Both little moons travel around Mars. Make two tiny shapes with your hands and move them around an imaginary planet.
Home again! Earth has one Moon, and Mars has two. We counted and explored together. Well done!
Our pretend rocket is looking for a giant striped planet. Let's visit Jupiter and see what we notice!
Jupiter is the biggest planet in our solar system. Stretch your arms wide, or make a big circle with your hands.
Jupiter's colorful stripes are bands of clouds. Trace an imaginary stripe from one side to the other.
Jupiter has no solid ground to stand on like Earth. We'll explore from our pretend spaceship instead of landing.
Light stripe, dark stripe! The clouds make wonderful patterns. What colors can you find in our picture?
Our pretend picture is home! Jupiter is a giant planet with cloud bands. You were a wonderful stripe spotter!
Our pretend spaceship is going to watch Jupiter from far above its clouds. Let's be gentle storm watchers!
Jupiter has a huge storm called the Great Red Spot. Can you find the spot on our planet picture?
The storm swirls around. Draw a slow circle in the air with one finger. Round and round!
Winds move Jupiter's clouds into bands. We stay in our pretend spaceship and watch from far away.
Jupiter is bigger than every other planet in our solar system. What a big world for a big storm!
We watched a giant planet and learned about its swirling storm. Our pretend adventure is safely home. Hooray!
Our pretend rocket has a special mission: find the planet with the beautiful rings. Let's visit Saturn!
Hello, Saturn! Its rings go around the planet. Make a wide ring with your arms or your fingers.
The rings are made of many pieces of ice and rock. They are not one solid hoop. Imagine lots of tiny pieces together.
We cannot walk on Saturn's rings like a road. Our pretend rocket watches from a safe distance.
Saturn is a giant planet without a solid surface like Earth's. We'll wave from our pretend spaceship.
Mission complete! Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock. You are a wonderful ring explorer!
Let's make a pretend space postcard for a friend. Our picture will show Saturn and its lovely rings!
Saturn is the second-biggest planet in our solar system. Jupiter is bigger. Our postcard needs room for a giant!
Its bright rings circle the planet. Trace a long, round shape in the air. What a lovely pretend drawing!
The rings contain lots of ice and rock pieces. Wiggle your fingers like many little pieces traveling together.
Our message says: hello from Saturn! We explored from our spaceship because Saturn has no solid ground like Earth.
Our pretend postcard has arrived! Tell a grown-up one thing you noticed about Saturn. Thank you, space artist!
Today our pretend rocket stays far from the Sun. We will learn about it through pictures. Ready to meet our special star?
The Sun is a star. It makes light and gives warmth to Earth. Our cheerful picture is pretending to smile!
Sunlight helps plants grow on Earth. Pretend your hands are little leaves opening in the light.
The real Sun is very hot. We never look straight at it. Our story picture is a safe way to explore together.
Our planet travels around the Sun. Imagine moving a little Earth around a big star. Around we go!
Thank you, Sun, for light and warmth! We learned that the Sun is a star. What a bright discovery!
A pretend little seed is waiting on Earth. What helps it grow? Let's follow the story of sunlight together.
The Sun sends light toward Earth. It is our nearest star. We use our story picture instead of looking at the real Sun.
With water, air, and light, many plants can grow. Pretend your little seed is stretching into a leafy plant.
The Sun makes its own light. The Moon does not. Moonlight is sunlight that bounces off the Moon.
Hello, Moon! You reflect sunlight. Our pretend plant and our shining Moon both remind us of the Sun.
Our little pretend plant has leaves! We learned about sunlight, our star, and reflected moonlight. Great discovering!
Choose a space adventure. Tap a picture, and we'll explore together!
